title: High-Frequency Micro-Inventory Updates for Urban Logistics
business: Urban logistics firms managing thousands of small, independent delivery lockers across a metropolitan area.
problem: The system suffers from data inconsistency and race conditions when multiple delivery agents attempt to claim the same locker compartment simultaneously, leading to double-bookings and failed deliveries.
solution: Implementing an Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) architecture using PostgreSQL allows for strict ACID compliance. By utilizing row-level locking and atomic transactions, the system ensures that once a locker is claimed, the state transition is isolated and durable, preventing concurrent processes from overwriting or conflicting with active reservations.
steps: Define a relational schema with a dedicated Lockers table containing a status column and a version identifier for optimistic concurrency control.
Encapsulate the reservation logic within a PL/pgSQL function to ensure the entire check-and-update operation executes as a single atomic unit.
Apply the SELECT ... FOR UPDATE clause within the transaction to lock the specific row, preventing other sessions from modifying the locker status until the current transaction commits or rolls back.
Configure the database connection pool to handle numerous short-lived connections efficiently, maintaining low latency for rapid transaction commits.
outcome: The system achieves reliable state consistency across all locker units, ensuring that every delivery assignment is unique and accurately reflected in the database without manual reconciliation.
limitation: The primary limitation is lock contention under extreme concurrency; if too many agents target the same locker simultaneously, transactions may wait or time out. This can be monitored by checking the pg_stat_activity view to identify blocked sessions and long-running transactions.

code.content:
BEGIN; -- Start atomic transaction
SELECT status FROM lockers WHERE id = 101 FOR UPDATE; -- Lock row for this agent
UPDATE lockers SET status = 'occupied' WHERE id = 101; -- Update state
COMMIT; -- Finalize and release lock
code.explanation: This snippet demonstrates an atomic transaction using row-level locking to prevent concurrent modification of a specific locker record.
